nodes.description: All five original patients had hypo- or agammaglobulinaemia, and B-cell lymphopenia is the lymphocyte defect common to the reported cases. In the milder 2024 patient it was the only lymphocyte abnormality found: T-cell counts, repertoire and proliferation and NK-cell number and function were normal. The severity of the B-cell deficiency does not follow the severity of the syndromic features.

nodes.description: Patients are homozygous for one of two splice-donor variants (c.638+36C>G, which creates a cryptic donor and a frameshift; c.103+2T>G, which inserts three amino acids in frame) or compound heterozygous for c.103+1G>T and the missense p.Cys301Arg. Every allele lowers PRIM1 protein without removing it entirely: full-length protein was 9-14% of wild type in c.638+36C>G cells, the C301R and V35insDGV products reached 25% and 52% in a reporter assay, and c.103+2T>G cells retained reduced protein.

nodes.description: PRIM1 is the catalytic subunit of the primase heterodimer, which forms a heterotetramer with the two DNA polymerase alpha subunits. It synthesises the RNA primers needed to start replication at origins and to start each Okazaki fragment. Depleting it is expected to reduce the efficiency of replication; the C301R substitution also sits next to the catalytic residue R304, and the equivalent change was lethal in yeast Pri1p.

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts double in about 49 hours against 23-27 hours for controls, and S phase lasts 16.6 hours against 6-7 hours. Wild-type PRIM1, but not C301R, rescues the long S phase. There was no increase in apoptotic or p21-positive cells, so the authors attribute the slow growth to delayed cell-cycle progression rather than cell death or cell-cycle exit. T-cell blasts from the milder 2024 patient instead showed more cells in S phase, which the authors suggest may reflect the same replication impairment in a faster-dividing cell type.
